data.name: Demo.welcome.Summary
data.value: The dossier, the dashboard and the menu.

data.name: Demo.welcome.intro.Text
data.value: Lettra is used to write quotes and invoices, and to prepare the accounting that goes with them. During this demo you are Atelier Numérique Conseil, a small consulting business. There is nothing to do: just watch, Lettra does the clicking.

data.name: Demo.welcome.dossier.Text
data.value: An accountant looks after many businesses. Each one has its own "dossier": its customers, its invoices, its accounts. This picker shows the open dossier; one dossier's data never mixes with another's.

data.name: Demo.welcome.revenue.Text
data.value: Revenue is the total the business has invoiced, excluding tax (that is, without VAT, which goes to the State). The dashboard follows it month by month, along with late invoices and quotes awaiting an answer.

data.name: Demo.welcome.menu.Text
data.value: Sales, customers, accounting, tax returns: every screen is grouped by topic. We will go through them in the order a business uses them.

data.name: Demo.company.Summary
data.value: The legal details printed on every invoice.

data.name: Demo.company.identity.Text
data.value: The SIREN is the 9-digit number the French State gives every business. It must appear on every invoice, with the name, address and legal form. Lettra adds them by itself.

data.name: Demo.company.vat.Text
data.value: VAT (value added tax) is a tax the business adds to its prices and then pays back to the State. Its EU VAT number identifies it for this tax across Europe.

data.name: Demo.company.terms.Text
data.value: How long customers have to pay, and the penalties if they pay late. The law requires them on invoices: Lettra adds them automatically.

data.name: Demo.customer.list.Text
data.value: These are the people and businesses Atelier Numérique Conseil sells its services to. Let's add a new one: a bakery in Lyon that wants digital training for its team.

data.name: Demo.customer.new.Text
data.value: We start with its name. Lettra can also look the business up in the official directory (SIRENE) to fill everything in at once; here we type by hand to see each field.

data.name: Demo.customer.siren.Text
data.value: For a business customer, its SIREN is mandatory: with the e-invoicing reform, it is used to route its invoices electronically. This number is fictitious, like all the demo data.

data.name: Demo.customer.address.Text
data.value: The address appears on the invoice, and the e-mail will be used to send invoices and, if needed, payment reminders. Lettra suggests the town as soon as you type the postcode.

data.name: Demo.customer.saved.Text
data.value: The customer sheet is ready. It will gather everything about this customer: quotes, invoices, what has been paid and what is still owed.

data.name: Demo.catalog.Summary
data.value: What you sell, with its price and VAT.

data.name: Demo.catalog.list.Text
data.value: This is the list of products and services the business sells, with their prices. You fill it in once, then pick from it to write quotes and invoices without retyping.

data.name: Demo.catalog.new.Text
data.value: A short reference to find it quickly, and a description: the text that will appear on the quote and the invoice.

data.name: Demo.catalog.price.Text
data.value: The price is entered excluding tax: that is what the business keeps. VAT (20% here) is added to get the price including tax, which the customer pays. So €450 excluding tax makes €540 including tax, of which €90 is VAT owed to the State.

data.name: Demo.catalog.saved.Text
data.value: The workshop is in the catalogue. Now let's offer it to our bakery.

data.name: Demo.quote.open.Text
data.value: A quote is a price proposal: it describes what will be done and how much it will cost. Until the customer accepts it, they owe nothing. We start from the customer sheet, so the customer is already chosen.

data.name: Demo.quote.subject.Text
data.value: One sentence summing up the proposal. It helps the customer understand what it is about, and helps you find the quote later.

data.name: Demo.quote.line.Text
data.value: Each line is one thing sold. We type the catalogue reference: description, price and VAT fill in by themselves. All that is left is the quantity: two workshops.

data.name: Demo.quote.totals.Text
data.value: Lettra calculates everything: €900 excluding tax, €180 VAT, €1,080 including tax. No arithmetic mistakes, and each VAT rate is broken down as the law requires.

data.name: Demo.quote.compliance.Text
data.value: Before validating, Lettra checks that every mandatory mention is there: both businesses' identities, numbers, dates, totals. One green tick per mention; if one were missing, the Validate button would stay greyed out.

data.name: Demo.quote.validate.Text
data.value: Validating gives the quote its final number, assigned in order with no gaps. It can no longer be changed: this is the document the customer receives.

data.name: Demo.quote.accept.Text
data.value: The bakery accepts the proposal. The quote becomes "Accepted" and can now turn into an invoice in one click, with nothing to retype.

data.name: Demo.invoice.Summary
data.value: The invoice, its number and its electronic version.

data.name: Demo.invoice.draft.Text
data.value: An invoice is the official request for payment. It copies the customer, subject and lines of the quote. Lettra adds the payment due date, worked out from the business's terms.

data.name: Demo.invoice.validate.Title
data.value: A validated invoice can no longer change

data.name: Demo.invoice.validate.Text
data.value: The law requires it: once validated, an invoice gets the number following the previous one, and it can no longer be changed or deleted. Lettra records it in a fraud-proof chain. To fix a mistake, you issue a "credit note", a kind of negative invoice.

data.name: Demo.invoice.qrcode.Text
data.value: As soon as it is validated, the invoice carries a payment QR code, on screen and on the PDF. The customer scans it with their banking app: the transfer opens already filled in, with the right IBAN, the right amount and the invoice number. Nothing to copy, and the payment is recognised on its own during bank reconciliation.

data.name: Demo.invoice.facturx.Text
data.value: Factur-X is a PDF a person can read that also carries the invoice data for software. It is one of the formats of the reform that makes e-invoicing mandatory between businesses in France.

data.name: Demo.invoice.issue.Text
data.value: With the reform, invoices between businesses go through a State-"approved platform", which delivers them to the customer and informs the tax authority. Here the platform is simulated: the invoice is filed and its tracking appears in the history.

data.name: Demo.payment.Summary
data.value: Record the customer's payment and link it to its invoice.

data.name: Demo.payment.new.Text
data.value: A "receipt" is money received from a customer. The bakery has made a bank transfer: we record it by choosing the customer. Lettra immediately shows the invoices not yet paid.

data.name: Demo.payment.allocate.Title
data.value: Which invoice is this payment for?

data.name: Demo.payment.allocate.Text
data.value: We type the amount received, €1,080. Lettra spreads it over the open invoice by itself. Linking a payment to its invoice is called "matching" (lettrage): it tells you at any time who still owes what.

data.name: Demo.payment.lettering.Text
data.value: The payment is recorded and the invoice is settled. Lettra has also written the matching accounting entry: we will find it in the journal.

data.name: Demo.bank.Summary
data.value: Compare the bank statement with what is recorded.

data.name: Demo.bank.import.Text
data.value: Regularly, you import the bank account statement (here a fictitious one). Lettra compares each transaction with the invoices and receipts it already knows.

data.name: Demo.bank.match.Text
data.value: For each statement line, Lettra suggests the matching payment or invoice; you confirm in one click. Reconciling means checking that the bank and the accounts tell the same story.

data.name: Demo.reminders.Summary
data.value: Politely remind customers of late invoices.

data.name: Demo.reminders.overview.Text
data.value: When a customer has not paid by the agreed date, the invoice is "overdue". This screen lists them all, with the days late and the amount still owed.

data.name: Demo.reminders.preview.Text
data.value: Lettra writes the reminder, from friendly to firm depending on how late it is, with the bank details to pay. You send it by e-mail, or note that you called instead. In the demo, no e-mail ever leaves your computer.

data.name: Demo.accounting.Summary
data.value: The entries Lettra wrote by itself.

data.name: Demo.accounting.journal.Text
data.value: Every invoice and every payment produces an "entry": debit and credit lines that always add up to the same total. Lettra wrote them all during the demo; the accountant has nothing to retype.

data.name: Demo.accounting.balance.Text
data.value: The trial balance adds up entries by account: 411 for what customers owe, 706 for sales of services, 44571 for VAT collected and owed, 512 for the bank. At a glance, the accountant sees whether everything balances.

data.name: Demo.tax.Summary
data.value: What the business must file, and when.

data.name: Demo.tax.vat.Text
data.value: Regularly, the business declares the VAT it charged its customers, minus the VAT it paid its suppliers. The difference is paid to the State. Lettra prepares the figures from the invoices.

data.name: Demo.tax.checks.Text
data.value: Forgotten drafts, invoices not sent, gaps with the accounts: Lettra flags anything that could make the return wrong before it is filed.

data.name: Demo.tax.calendar.Text
data.value: VAT, corporate tax, business property tax (CFE): each tax has its deadlines. The calendar gathers them so nothing is forgotten, and you tick off what is done.

data.name: Demo.fec.Summary
data.value: The file the tax authority can ask for.

data.name: Demo.fec.export.Text
data.value: During a tax audit, the business must hand over all its accounts in a file in the official format, the FEC. Lettra produces it in one click and checks it before downloading.

data.name: Demo.cabinet.Summary
data.value: The accountant's view across all dossiers.

data.name: Demo.cabinet.overview.Text
data.value: Let's switch viewpoint: this is the accountant's screen. All the dossiers the firm looks after are gathered here, with what needs attention: late invoices, VAT to file, bank to reconcile.

data.name: Demo.cabinet.prevention.Text
data.value: The firm also spots businesses that could soon run short of cash: a balance that drops below zero, customers paying later and later, VAT heavier than the money coming in. Each dossier gets a level (calm, watch, call the client) worked out by simple rules, with no artificial intelligence. It helps decide whether to call the owner: the radar decides nothing and is never shown to the client.

data.name: Demo.cabinet.pilotage.Text
data.value: Simple indicators to steer the business, such as how long customers take to pay on average or the share of quotes accepted. Everyone only sees the dossiers they are allowed to.

data.name: Demo.end.Summary
data.value: Recap and ideas to explore on your own.

data.name: Demo.end.done.Text
data.value: Customer, quote, e-invoice, payment, bank, reminders, accounting, VAT and firm overview: that is the full life of a sale. Everything the demo created stays in the dossier. The "?" button at the top answers your questions, and Ctrl+K finds any screen.

data.name: Demo.ai.Summary
data.value: What Lettra's AI does, what it never does, and how to turn it off.

data.name: Demo.ai.guide.Text
data.value: Everything you have just seen happened without AI: rules, calculations and checks are written into Lettra. The AI assistant is off by default; a firm administrator can turn it on and choose which features to open.

data.name: Demo.ai.never.Text
data.value: The AI explains and suggests, you decide: it never approves, issues or sends a document, and never sees the dossier's names, which are replaced by tokens before anything is sent.

data.name: Demo.ai.registry.Text
data.value: Each AI use is listed with its risk level under the European AI regulation and its status in this dossier. Further down, the log records every request, engine call and failure.
